result.rationale: The diff changes deleteEvent (and updateEvent) from `const calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.externalId;` to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. In the falsy-externalCalendarId branch, the find predicate compares against the falsy externalCalendarId, so it can never match, always yielding undefined — the fallback to destinationCalendar's externalId is lost, so calendarId is undefined in a case the old code handled. This is a verifiable dead-predicate defect introduced by the diff.

judged_text: `deleteEvent` uses the same dead predicate: when `externalCalendarId` is falsy it evaluates `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`, which is always undefined because externalCalendarId is falsy in that branch. Cancelling bookings whose reference lacks externalCalendarId attempts a delete against calendarId undefined, leaving orphaned events on the host's Google Calendar that the previous code (which fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`) would have deleted.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the new fallback for `selectedCalendar`/`calendarId` is incorrect. In both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent`, when `externalCalendarId` is falsy the code does `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`, but `externalCalendarId` is falsy in that branch so the predicate can never match a real `externalId`, yielding `undefined`. This removes the previous fallback behavior (to the event’s destination calendar externalId) and will prevent deleting/updating events that were created on a non-primary destination calendar when the booking reference lacks `externalCalendarId`, leading to orphaned events.
